messages.text: Randy-boy, I found two shiny quarters in my purse. Want me to bring them Sunday?
Yes put them in the pink one! Mama said not opening it yet.
That's fine. We can just drop them in and listen to the clink.
I want the ladder truck picture one day.
Rain is loud over the shop. Tell Randy I put his yellow truck by the door for show-and-tell.
I heard BOOM and got under Mama blanket but I am wearing shoes now.
Good. Count five rumbles with Mama, then carry the truck in your backpack.
I counted. I am going to school. My truck is in the front pocket.
Coach said the blue cone drill was hard today, but you got back in line for another turn.
I found the blue racer with the back wheel hanging off. Leave it on the kitchen counter till I get home.
I wanted the ball to go by the cone. It went sideways.
Can I watch the little silver thing turn it open?
Then you watched the next kid's foot and changed where yours went. Good noticing.
After supper. You can hold the cup for the tiny screws and we will see where that wheel goes.
Next time I put my foot like this. Also the cone was leaning.
I made it a garage with blocks so it can wait.
I put the school update sheet in your folder. I marked the same boxes as last year and left the extra-language line blank.
Did I get a sticker for my folder?
Yes, baby. Just hand it to Ms. Kim when you get to class. The reading paper is in there too.
I turned the living room volume low while supper finished. If Randy asks, just tell him some grown-ups were upset downtown and we still use kind hands at school.
Mama why was the truck lights blue and red
They help keep the road clear. You can draw your fire station after bath, okay? ❤️
I want the ladder one
I put your dinosaur crayons on the coffee table and I am right by the couch. Bring your blue blanket if the thunder gets loud. ❤️
I want to sit by you and draw the big cloud.
Come here, sweet boy. Two slow breaths with me, then we can make the cloud silly.
Can my LEGOs sit on the rug too
Randy can you bring the blue truck one tomorrow? Mason says he has the red crayon this time.
I made big circles for the wheels and a long tail one with teeth.
Mason says make a road too. He wants to race after snack.
Ok I put blocks on it like a garage.
Mason says: bring the yellow dump truck by the block rug tomorrow?
I can ask Mama. Mrs. Bell said only one toy in backpacks.
My truck lost the black circle thing. Mama said ask Randy if he knows where it goes 🚚
I can look. I got my yellow spiral by me.
His mama says okay, just put your name sticker on it.
Mason says Randy can show him the red furry letter video tomorrow if their tablets are out.
Mom says tell Randy I want the big dump truck tomorrow.
Daddy can find the sticker after supper.
I want the A one and the snowman sing one.
I can use it first bell then Mason after timer. Not all day.
Send picture. Mine has one silver dot and one tiny hole.
His mama said only after centers if Mrs. Cole says yes. He wants the truck video too.
I drawed the wheel spot and put a arrow. Bring it tomorrow.
Ok and I get the red blocks too?
Some red blocks for your road and some for my bridge.
No truck. The ice song first.
Randy-boy, I found that old bag of purple and green beads in my closet. Want me to bring some Sunday?
Yes and the shiny cup from the big wagon people.
I remember you sitting on the curb with your little ear covers. You waved hard when the tall flower wagon came by.
I waved like Elsa.
I put your blue cleats by the back door. Try not to climb the porch rail while Mama gets supper going.
I only went up two steps and then kicked the ball to the fence.
Two steps is plenty. Tomorrow we can time you from the steps to the pecan tree after homework.
I want the little numbers to be smaller this time.
I saved the tall white slopes from that magazine. We can look after supper.
Can my little boots go there? I want to step in it.
Found your little blue bucket behind the mower. Still has two flat rocks and that curly leaf in it.
Maybe one day. Tonight we can make the road go up high with the brick pieces.
Save it Daddy. I need it for tiny white shells too.
And a big red house with doors for the loud truck.
I rinsed the mud off. If we go by the low water Saturday, you can look, but shoes stay tied.
And listen for the loud ribbit ones.
We can walk after supper if the gnats settle down. Stay by the yard road and do not go past the pond.
I want the part by the school fence where the frogs make noise.
Shoes first. If Mr. Ray rolls by in his pickup, wave from the driveway only.
Can we stop at the little park and look if they put the tall slide yet?
Mason said he will race trucks after centers. His mama asks if Randy is bringing the blue paper back today.
Mama put it in my folder. I did the ouch thing and got a dinosaur sticker.
He says dinosaur sticker is fast. Mrs. Cole said clean hands before snack again.
I used soap because Mrs. Cole checks thumbs.
Mason says the big red truck came by school today and the man let us see the shiny hat.
I drawed the ladder. Mrs. Reed said stand on the yellow line and wait turns.
He waved when the bus left. Mason wants the loud horn next time.
Mama said tell Daddy so we can build one with blocks.
Mason said Randy can have the blue crayon tomorrow if Mason gets the dump truck first.
I pick red sticker one. Mama said I do not get the table sticker.
Mason says stickers are for moms and dads. Kids get treasure box stickers.
I want treasure box truck sticker then.
Did you get your little reader bag zipped up before Mama came?
Yes and I put blocks back at centers. I only had to go back for the blue one.
Good job. What was on your tray today?
The twisty noodles with yellow stuff. I ate lots and did my number page.
Ask Randy if he is bringing the red car tomorrow. We can race it from the porch to the pecan tree.
I bring red car and my fast shoes. I hide behind the shed first.
Mama said after lunch, when the grownups are done talking. Mason better not get all the blocks at school Monday.
I tell Mason the blue truck is mine at recess.
You did better at the car line today. I saw you wave before I pulled away ❤️
I still wanted you but I held the blue book.
Ms. Landry wrote that you put your folder in the basket by yourself after morning bell.
Mason showed me where the crayons go.
I put your blue shorts by the door with the tall socks.
And my little black shoes?
Yes. After breakfast we go to the field, so bedtime stays early tonight.
Coach said look first then kick.
Bath is done, pajamas next, then two pages from the little book. Your loader book is already in the branch bag for tomorrow. ❤️
I did cow by myself and the word dig.
You sure did. After lights, the book bag stays by the door so we can grab it after breakfast.
Then shoes then folder then truck book.
I put your black socks and shin guards on the bench. Cleats are beside them.
I found one guard. Other one was under the truck blanket.
Good catch. Hands at the sink after cereal, then we can head to the field.
Ok Daddy. I got the orange cup too.
I put the envelope from the mailbox by Mama's coffee cup. Don't draw on that one, bud.
Can I draw fire truck on my paper instead?
Yep. Use your dinosaur pad. Mama and I will finish the grown-up papers after breakfast.
I want the big ladder truck when we go store.
Your green jersey is on the dryer. Shoes are still muddy from practice.
I want my team shirt and my folder too
We will pack both. Mama said lay out your nice pants before bed for tomorrow morning.
Can I clap on the fast song again?
Bath first, then two books. I put your shoes by the door for the morning.
Can I pick the truck book and sleep with red dino?
Yes. Folder is already signed, and your lunch is packed with the applesauce you like. ❤️
I made Mason a tiny road picture.
Mason wants to send his fastest dump truck picture. Can Randy see it?
Mama says send it here. I don't have the place with buttons and hearts.
Okay. Mason says show him the truck after your puzzle thing.
I did 8 and 9 and then the bell noise said stop.
Randy-boy, I saved a little bowl of beans and rice after church if you come by.
I want that and apple slices please.
I can do that. I put a dab of butter on the green beans too, just how you took two bites last time.
I'm by the shed if Randy wants the little bucket. We can look under the log by the pine.
I want bugs and the flat rock!
Okay. Boots first, and you stay where I can tap your shoulder.
I won't go past the shiny puddle place.
Can Randy bring the blue car after church? I want to race it down the porch board.
Mama says porch only. I can push it after Daddy puts it on the board first.
Ok I will count. The fast noise is the best part.
I want to see if it jumps at the crack. Then Mama says snack.
Can I race you from porch to tree after church? Mama said we leave before supper.
Yes! I get my red truck and my room rug road.
Aunt Laura said put the game pieces back in your bin before Uncle Daniel gets home.
Daddy knows where the tiny wheel goes.
Bedtime soon. Please put the loose screws back in the little cup before they roll under the table.
I put 3 by the blue car picture in my yellow book.
Good job keeping them together. Daddy can see your page after teeth.
Tell him I know which one goes by the back tire.
Mama said the red tower fell over after school. I saved the flat pieces for you on the kitchen table.
I cried on Mama and made a mad scribble.
That happens. After supper we can build it wider, like a bridge.
You do the bottom and I do the little cars.
Bath first, then pajamas. I put the little bandage box back under the sink from your outside tumble.
My knee has the blue one. It looks like a sticker.
It can stay tonight. Backpack only needs folder and cup tomorrow, nothing extra for the teacher.
Can I bring my dinosaur picture too?
Mama says we can ride together to the Quitman field if your mama says yes.
I can bring my blue truck and my shoes.
She also said the coach needs the same paper with 8-14-20 written on it. Mine has numbers too.
Mama has mine in the folder from the Ruston place.
Your teacher sent a note that you asked why the ramp made the marble slow down.
Because the tape was bumpy. I fixed one side.
Same face you made Saturday when the ball skipped past your shoe. You stopped, looked down, and checked your feet.
My shoe was not pointing at the goal.
Randy-boy, I am bringing the big spoon you liked last time. Your mama said the pot has to sit a bit first.
Randy-boy, I found a big yellow backhoe book and one with baby goats at the Jonesboro sale table.
I can do it when it don't make steam.
Bring goats. Mama said snack then folder then outside.
That's right. We will let the grownups fuss with the hot part, then you can give it a good slow turn.
I will. Sunday you can show me that STOP sign word you told me about.
Eli can see me and then we eat outside?
I know stop and red.
Randy-boy, did Mama let you have your little screen after supper?
Yes Grandma. I picked the snow one and then Cookie ate cookies.
Well goodness. Just one more song, then listen to Mama and rest your eyes.
I put the red fire truck wheel back on. It is on the kitchen table.
Can I show Mason before Mrs. Bell rings the clean-up bell?
Ask Mama when she checks your folder. If it goes, it stays zipped until rug time.
I want him to see the ladder go up.
I left the tiny screwdriver in the top drawer. Only with me sitting there, bud.
The yellow car has a loose wheel. I made where the screw goes on my paper.
Good eye. We can look at the axle after supper, then put your brick bridge back.
And the big gray chompy one can go under the bridge.
I saw that red LEGO fire station box at the store. We can look at the picture after supper.
Can we get it today?
Not today, bud. Put the dime Grandma gave you in the little bank and we'll mark one more square.
Okay. Do I get a cookie for helping shoes too?
He wandered off when the couch talk got too serious. Found him lining up rescue trucks by the LEGO bridge.
That sounds right. I just told him some people needed calm voices and then asked about his school helper chart.
He said tomorrow he can share the red crayon with Mason if Mason is mad.
And my truck goes wee-woo by the bridge
Mama says we can race after church Sunday if it ain't raining.
Are you coming Sunday? I can beat you porch to tree.
My teacher had elephant signs and donkey signs on the board. I said elephant wins because it is bigger.
I want to show you the cone game. The whistle man stopped cars for us at the parade.
Yes. Daddy said my arm is okay for running now.
I like elephant too but dinosaur bigger.
We can put sticks like cones from porch to tree.
Grandma said grown folks pick names, not animals. I still think elephant.
And my fire truck can sit by the finish.
My mom said no dirt hands before food.
I pick T rex name.
My teacher says bubbles on fingers and Daddy says listen when Dr. Nguyen says stuff.
Mama said bring your family tree page Sunday. Mine has Pawpaw, Mawmaw, and the old Dodd picture by the church steps.
Mine has Mama and Daddy and Grandma Betty. I drew the porch too.
Good. Aunt Laura said help Randy say the names just like we practice at home, not the song from TV.
I can say Dodd real loud.
Backpack is packed: folder, clean shirt, and snack. Shoes are by the couch.
Can I get the green robot too?
Not today, sweetheart. We already got what you needed for school.
Ok I can show Daddy my truck picture.
Ms. Henry said you helped at blocks today. What did you say?
I said put the long ones back in middle so Carter can make roof.
That was kind. Did the bucket stay on the table?
Yes. Teacher moved our clips when the sand ran out.
Last Elsa song, then brush teeth. I already moved it back to the kitchen charger.
Can I have one more Elsa please please?
Not tonight, baby. You can pick a book with Olaf on the cover.
Okay. I want the snow book.
My mama says can you bring the red truck tomorrow?
I ask Mama. I have folder paper too.
We can make dirt roads after snack if teacher lets us.
I bring blue crayon for signs.
Mason says he got to the red slide first today.
My mom says bring your truck picture tomorrow. We get red crayon first.
No I touched the pole then went up the ladder!
I have to put my folder in the backpack first. Mama said no forgetting.
Did you choose the orange noodles at lunch?
He says tomorrow do it from the chalk line to the big tree.
Yes. Then Ms. Tate helped me read the tiny sentence with Sam.
Okay and after we kick by the fence.
Mason says can Randy bring the race truck tomorrow?
Not that one. Daddy said it has a loose wheel and the inside round part has to stay on the towel.
He wants to see the round part at recess but his mom says no tiny pieces in backpacks.
I can draw it. It goes around when the wheel goes around.
My mama says ask Randy if he wants to race trucks by the fence tomorrow.
My mom says can Randy wear old shoes tomorrow? We are doing mud roads by the fence.
Yes and I know where to hang my bag now.
Mama said my gray ones. And my folder goes in first.
We sit near the blocks after bell if Ms. Landry says quiet hands.
Bring the green truck picture if you can.
After teeth I can show Mama where it is.
I did not need my book after snack today.
Randy-boy, I found two more quarters in my purse. Still saving for that big box with the station walls?
Yes. It needs a pole and a tall ladder and a bridge too.
Your mama said you drew little people waiting by the water. That ladder better reach.
I make them get out safe then I make the bridge strong.
I fixed the little bench by the ditch. Wait till the sun drops before you climb around it.
My legs stick to the seat when it is shiny hot.
Yep. We will spray your ankles too. Frogs are already loud by the pond.
Can you make a pretend long slide with boards from porch to grass?
Aunt Laura said bring your bucket Sunday. I found a gray rock shaped like a chip.
I got a leaf with points. I want a shell like Grand Isle.
The ones that crunch? You had sand stuck all in your shoes last time you told me.
Yes and Mama shook them outside.
Mason says he saved the yellow dump truck for Randy if he comes Monday.
I come Monday! Coach said kick with inside foot tomorrow.
His mom says maybe after the game you can show him that tree race Eli keeps talking about.
Eli goes too fast but I can beat him if I start by the steps.
My tower fell loud today 😂
Mine made a big clack. Mrs. Nora put one block sideways and I did the tall part.
Tomorrow do the ramp one.
Yes but only center time. I want the truck to bump down it.
Randy-boy, I found two quarters for your piggy bank. Tell your mama I will bring them Sunday.
My bank is on my shelf by dinosaurs.
Good. I won't bring the fold-up bed this time since we are just eating cake and heading back.
Daddy said cake after lunch, not before.
Randy-boy, Mama sent me that picture of you in the green shirt by the nets.
I almost made it go in!
You keep listening to that man with the whistle. Watch it close and try again, baby.
Are y'all staying at your house after church or going to Grandma's?
Mama said we are coming back to Quitman first so I can get my LEGOs.
Bring the car one. Aunt Laura said she found your little hospital card in the Ruston box when she got the 8/14/20 copy.
It has tiny feet on it. I want to show Grandma.
Bring the beads after church? We can make the block road for the big carts.
I make Canal Street and the yellow one throws cups.
Then I get the fire truck like July. You sing the snow song when it drives by.
Only if I get red blocks too.
Can Randy come race from porch to tree after lunch?
Mama says yes when she brings her chair outside.
Bring the jar. I found tiny shells in the dirt by the roots.
No road side. Mama points with her finger.
Mama said we can race after the grownups finish eating tomorrow.
I go sit by Grandma then sing then race you
The hand-clap one better happen. Last time you were louder than me.
We can walk by the pink spun-sugar stand after the school fair games, but supper comes first.
Mac bowl first then pink fluffy cup?
Corn with the mac bowl, then a small cup. Deal?
Deal and no big spoon.
Randy-boy looked peppy after church. I was glad that runny nose from last weekend was gone.
I ran from the porch to the tree faster than Eli.
You sure did. Tell Mama I did not see anything that needs a doctor bag, just grass on those shoes.
We made the porch-to-tree line. Come race after lunch.
Is the big brown dog by the fence still doing WOOF WOOF?
Aunt Laura said we can use the other side yard. I will stand by the gate.
Okay I am bringing my red car. I can run from the steps.
Randy-boy, your daddy showed me the little goal you made with blocks.
It fell down when the ball hit it.
He said you put the tall blocks on the sides the next time.
Then it stayed. I want Eli to kick soft first.
Mama says we coming Saturday after church clothes shopping. Can we race porch to the tree before everyone eats?
Yes and I get first turn by the cooler.
Only if you don't spill the red cups again. My dad said there will be lots of shells on the paper.
I want the corn and the loud song.
Randy-boy, your mama said you got quiet after the big whistle at school. Grandma can bring the farm stickers Sunday.
I sat by Mama and did my little breaths.
That sounds just right. You can show me the sticker page after church.
I want to draw the tractor one.
Randy-boy, your mama showed me the little family page. That old cemetery picture has Dodds clear back on both sides.
Grandma I read my book words tonight.
I heard you did. Keep sounding them out the way Mama reads with you before bed.
Mrs. Bell sent home the green note. You and Mason need to bring the block rug trucks back to the shelf tomorrow.
We made a road by the cubbies.
I saw. After snack we will put your folder in the backpack, then you can tell Daddy about it.
Tell Daddy the big truck got stuck.
Randy-boy saw that storm map at my house and wanted to know if the red part was coming to Quitman.
Thank you for keeping it on the map. He gets stuck on sirens and flashing trucks if the other clips stay on.
I told him we listen to Mama, stay sweet at school, and let the big folks handle the loud stuff.
Grandma I colored the storm red and blue
Randy-boy, your mama sent me that picture at the table. What were all those little pieces?
The red car tummy. Daddy made the tiny screw come out and I held the flashlight.
Well keep those pieces in the bowl, sugar. Grandma does not want one hiding under your foot.
I saw little teeth move when the tire moved.
Mama said you asked if your name goes on the paper at the church hall. That table is for the big folks today, bud.
I can write R and D.
You sure can. You can write it on your dinosaur page after breakfast.
Can I get round sticker if I write neat?
I found red bricks for your station roof. We can put the doors on after supper.
Can we make a place for the water hose and the hat?
Yep. Mama said Dr. Bell gave you a sticker, too. Tough kid.
Tablet is charged. Ask Mama before you tap anything.
Can I do the let it go one?
One song after you put the LEGO bin lid on. Then maybe the little counting clip.
The sticker has a star. I show Grandma and put the truck by it.
I want the count man laugh.
I want all the blue bricks when we come Sunday.
No all. Blue bricks stay in pile and we pick some.
What if I am building the biggest tower?
Then Mama can do timer like school.
Good morning, buddy. Dr. Nguyen signed your yellow card, and I put it in the front pocket of your backpack. ❤️
Is there another pinch today?
No, not today. Just folder day. Daddy read the note too, and Mrs. Cole will collect it.
Okay. I will give it to Mrs. Cole after breakfast.
Bath first, then one show. When the timer rings, tablet goes on the counter.
But I want the truck video and the blue bricks video.
Pick one tonight. You did good putting blocks away, so choose a dinosaur sticker before bed.
Sticker on my paper and coins stay closed?
Randy-boy, I put two quarters by your plate. Eli is already asking who gets to count to ten by the laundry room.
I count first! No peeking. I want the quarters for my truck bank.
Laura said shoes before you run outside. Daniel can help with that loose wheel after supper.
That red truck clicks again because the little spring jumped out. Want me to save it in the parts cup?
Yes and don't throw it away. I need to make the spring page.
Got it. I'll leave the tiny screwdriver on the counter when I get home.
I can show you where the click sound was.
After lunch race from porch to the big pine?
Only if we do not go by the wet grass. Bugs bite me there.
Ok. We can go road side and wave at Uncle Mark's truck.
Then let's draw the slide in dirt where it should go.
Mama said we can go outside after lunch. I call porch to oak tree.
I call the short way by the swing and then I get the ball.
No shortcut. Touch the oak, then back to the porch, then kicks.
I am going to beat you when my shoes are tied tight.
Aunt Laura said you can bring the car box after church. I call porch to tree first.
I am bringing the one with no door and my brick ramp.
Bring paper too so we can make maps for the dirt road.
I need green for the spiky back and black for tire marks.
We packed your blue coat for the pretend trip game at school Monday. Do you want the puffy boots picture too?
Yes and the tall white rocks picture.
Okay. After lunch, Daddy can help you make the long crossing so the toy people can get over.
Put the red truck by it. It helps when they are stuck.
Randy can we make dirt roads after lunch? I got my dump truck.
Yes. I am bringing 3 rocks and the bumpy brown leaf.
My mom said stay away from the ditch water.
Okay but if the frogs talk I can hear them from the grass.
Randy-boy, the church class is in the little room today, not your regular one. I saved you a seat by me.
New room? Is Mama coming to the door?
She can walk you in, and I have two quarters for your pocket after class.
I went in. I sat by the window and did the glue paper.
I saved two little wheels and a flat board for your rolling stage build.
Can it have a mask face and green gold stuff?
Yep. We can tape the beads on after your choir shirt comes out of the dryer.
And Elmo rides by the ice queen.
Mama says yall are bringing leftovers after church. Are you bringing the yellow noodles?
Yes and I get the corner with cheese.
I saved you a banana from our table if you race me first.
Race then banana then cars.
Randy-boy, Mama sent me the picture of your green folder star. You looked proud.
I walked in with Mason and put my lunch in the tub.
That is big. Did you still keep that little book in your hand?
Only in the car. Ms. Landry read one and then I did centers.
I set the dump truck book beside your bed. Mama said page 3 has three words you can try before she finishes it.
I try dump. Then Mama reads the long part.
Good deal. Tomorrow morning it is breakfast, shoes, blue folder, then truck picture in your cubby.
And no skipping folder.
Can we do porch-to-tree race then kick in the yard Sunday?
Yes. I get two kicks if the first one goes wrong.
Okay but you have to move the sticks for the goal again.
I know where they go now. The skinny stick bends too much.
Are you coming after church Sunday? We can race porch to tree.
Mama says yes if my shoes stay clean.
Bring your fire truck. I got two quarters for your bank if Grandma says okay.
I want the ladder one. I put coins in the blue pig.
Can Randy send me his dinosaur drawing where everybody can see it?
Mama says only this message. I can send the picture to you.
Fine. Come race when that number game is done.
It beeped. I asked for 5 more but Mama said shoes on.
Randy-boy, Grandma found two quarters for your piggy bank. I will bring them Sunday after church.
I save for red LEGO truck!
Good saving. Ask Mama where to put them when I visit, and keep your school shoes out of the mud.
Mama says shoes stay by door and my clothes are clean.
Randy-boy, did they have your favorite hot tray today or did Mama pack food?
Hot tray. Yellow noodles. I cleaned my spot too.
That sounds fine. Show me those letters when I come Sunday.
I can do R and D and put my papers in the bag.
Laura told me the office finally took the papers. Did they spell Randy-boy right?
Yes Grandma. Mama said it says Dodd and Quitman.
Good. I still remember driving over by Ruston when you were tiny, and now that 08/14/20 line is on every school thing.
Randy-boy, your mama sent me the picture of you by the church trees with mud on both shoes.
Randy-boy, your mama showed me the fridge paper. Those round tires were something else.
I found tadpoles and the road dust made my socks brown.
Can I get coins when you come Sunday?
It has a ladder and little bolts. The orange one is chasing it.
Randy-boy, I found that round sticker stuck on my purse from the school gym day.
Save it for me Sunday. I found two shiny coins for your jar.
Next time I will bring wipes and that spray for your legs. Maybe the air will feel like pumpkin time soon.
You picked? Did you pick red or blue?
Pumpkin air is best for running. I still need a slide that goes fast.
I picked a person, sugar. The red and blue were just colors on signs.
I pick fire truck color.
I will show you my new brick station too.
I packed the overnight bag for Grandma's: pajamas, toothbrush, blue cup, and the green truck.
The office sent back Randy's packet. They only needed my signature under the same household info Laura filled in.
Thank you. Add the small bandages because he keeps racing on that driveway.
Daddy can we build the red fire station?
Done. No other little bottles or papers in the kitchen basket.
After supper. And bring me that library book so we can read the truck page before lights out.
I am bringing the fast truck.
I know the word ladder.
Can Randy bring the red car tomorrow after breakfast?
Mama said after pajamas and teeth I can put it by my backpack.
Wear fast shoes. We race porch to tree.
Daddy said not the shiny ones if grass is wet.
Randy, Daddy put your shell cup on the back steps. You can show Grandma after supper. ❤️
I got a yellow leaf and a bumpy shell.
Good. Remember our spot: porch, oak, flower bed. You stop if you can't see me.
And I call you for the scary rope thing.
One puzzle before pajamas. I will turn the first corner piece, then you finish the road.
I want the dump truck piece because it makes the road go curvy.
Deal. When the little song ends, pieces go back in the box.
Ok I do the road fast and then hear the song.
I put your jar on the dresser. Only two shells, one shiny rock, and the little leaf tonight, okay?
Can the frog picture go by it?
Yes. The one from the tent trip is dry now. We will tape it after pajamas.
The water was loud and the frogs were louder.
Mrs. Keller wrote that you used the quiet corner today, then finished your turtle picture. I am proud of your trying. ❤️
I wanted you at school but she helped me count.
I know. Daddy put the fire station pieces by your bed for after pajamas.
Can you hug me before the story
Mason wants to know if Randy saw the fire truck on TV yesterday.
I saw a big ladder and then Mama said go get blocks
He says build the road at school Monday.
Ok and I will not grab the red crayon
Mom says we can meet at the new playground by the ball field at 5:45.
I never went there. Are the tall slides loud?
We can start with trucks in the sand first. I brought the dump truck.
My mom says I can bring the dump truck tomorrow if your mama says okay.
Mama said outside first. Daddy cuts grass.
I am coming. Mama said sand first then slide.
Can we make roads in your yard and put the trucks by your door?
Yes but the blue bucket goes back in my closet after you go.
My mom said pancakes before Saturday soccer. Are you having those too?
Yes pancakes and cereal if Mama says little bowl.

events.title: Morning service, then cousins
events.notes: Bring blue folder from Randy's room, clean shoes, and soccer cleats in case the kids play outside after lunch.

events.title: Randy: shoes, folder, blue jacket
events.notes: Put folder in backpack before breakfast. Blue jacket by the door. Teeth before leaving.

events.title: Morning backpack run
events.notes: Laura packs lunch and folder. Daniel checks shoes by the door. Booster seat stays in Daniel's truck after drop-off.

events.title: Picture cards before school
events.notes: Put backpack by chair, shoes under bench, blue folder in front pocket. Add branch bag with excavator book and deer-tracks book; leave the short page book on the nightstand for later.

events.title: Pack Randy lunch
events.notes: Sandwich halves, banana, corn cup, and blue cereal bowl left by the lunchbox.

events.title: Backpack, folder, lunchbox check
events.notes: Blue folder signed by Laura. Put snack cup in front pouch, dinosaur drawing in folder, and piggy-bank quarter back on dresser.

events.title: Morning folder, tray money, backpack check
events.notes: Sign green sheet, add spare shirt, practice the M page once, remind him to pick the orange elbow noodles if they have them.

events.title: Randy drop-off, Room 4
events.notes: Pack blue folder, lunch box, and the small dinosaur book. Ms. Landry said he can keep it on the table until carpet time.

events.title: Randy - nurse room after school
events.notes: Bring blue school form. Laura note: numbing spray request, sit on Mama's lap first, sticker after.

events.title: Porch-to-oak treasure cup
events.notes: Cup on porch rail. Pick 3 leaves and 2 smooth rocks between steps and big oak while Mama folds clothes outside. Stop before the gravel strip.

events.title: Pick up Randy from gym-side after grown-up line clears
events.notes: Bring backpack and crayons. He wanted one of the round red-white-blue stickers from the table; reminder that those were for the adults coming through the line.

events.title: Blue folder forms with Laura
events.notes: Laura signs the school packet, adds Daniel's work number, clips the lunch slip behind it, and writes the three names used for home pickup.

events.title: Randy: timer after bath
events.notes: Letters, counting, one puzzle. Keep kid folder open. Stop when kitchen timer rings.

events.title: Turn in school nurse page
events.notes: Laura signed. Daily-at-school line left N/A. Past-year boxes left blank except sniffles, one warm-forehead day, playground knee scrape.

events.title: Drop packet at Quitman Elementary office
events.notes: Bring blue folder, shot copy with 08/14/20 line, and parish paper from the Ruston folder.

events.title: Toy car table time
events.notes: Daniel opens first tiny screw. Randy handles the others on the towel tray. Stop when Mama's oven timer rings.

events.title: Randy drop-off: folder, lunch, one small truck
events.notes: Blue folder signed. Tell Mrs. Bell Randy and Mason both asked for the block rug bin.

events.title: Kindergarten center chart
events.notes: Blocks table: name clips move after sand timer. Keep extra pieces in middle basket.

events.title: Drop off kindergarten update packet
events.notes: Bring folder page with household boxes signed; no second-language form needed. Ask office to copy the page before pickup line.

events.title: Shin guards + cleats at the park
events.notes: Pack water bottle. Coach wants the kids watching the ball before they kick.

events.title: Saturday kids soccer
events.notes: Bring water, size 3 ball, and the small pump. Coach's station: two tries at cone gate, then help reset cones before snack.

events.title: Saturday field time
events.notes: Bring shin guards, water bottle, small towel. Let Randy do two short goal-box turns before snack.

events.title: Quitman parade on Main Street
events.location: Main Street by the church lot, Quitman, LA
events.notes: Bring folding chairs. Stand near crosswalk so Randy can watch the cones and the red truck go by.

events.title: Kitchen table bin + yard time
events.notes: Set out brick tub, small cars, paper, crayons. Save green and gray. Shoes by back door after lunch.

events.title: Kitchen table parts tray with Daniel
events.notes: Use muffin tin for tiny pieces. Blue bricks box can stay out. Old red car from top shelf only if Daniel is sitting there.

events.title: Randy: count jar coins after cartoons
events.notes: Only count and write the number on the notepad. Put coins back before toy aisle trip. Sticker sheet ready for room cleanup.

events.title: Eli over - big pot on back burner
events.notes: Put Randy's little stool by the counter only after the burner is off. Cousins can run outside before supper.

events.title: Supper prep: switch TV to weather before Randy comes in
events.notes: Keep explanation short if he asks about loud street clips. Mention helpers, then blocks or dinosaurs.

events.title: Randy tablet turn
events.notes: After pajamas and teeth. One singing video with the ice castle girl or one short red-puppet counting clip, then plug it back in.

events.title: Quitman Baptist, Betty's table, yard time
events.location: Quitman Baptist / Betty Dodd's house, Jonesboro
events.notes: Pack quiet book, spare shirt, small LEGO box. Eli and Randy outside after plates are cleared if the ground is dry.

events.title: Walk by parish pond with Randy
events.notes: Bring small bag, bug wipes, old sneakers. Randy wants smooth rocks, red leaves, and a quiet spot near the water.

events.title: Library craft table: winter peaks + brick tower photos
events.notes: Bring blue mittens from drawer, small camera, and the block bridge picture for show-and-tell wall.

events.title: Church yard visit with cousins
events.location: Quitman church lot, by back trees
events.notes: Bring water, bug spray, and Randy's sneakers. Check small play area after service; he asked about the higher slide again.

events.title: Print Randy pictures for show table
events.notes: Choose 3: Canal Street curb photo with bead cup, church robe picture, red-white-blue truck line from last summer. No glitter pages in school folder.

events.title: Randy checkup before kindergarten drop-off
events.notes: Bring blue dinosaur sticker sheet. Hold hand for finger pinch and bandage. Drop off by 9:15 with backpack and lunchbox.

events.title: Green folder note for Mrs. Keller
events.notes: Pack small sketch pad. If morning gets rough, art table first, slow counting, then Laura can step into the hall before work.

events.title: Kitchen table: small car pieces
events.notes: Use towel, cup for screws, yellow spiral, tape for one loose spring. Let Randy make the before/after page.

events.title: Pick up Randy - front awning
events.notes: Bring signed reading sheet and the yellow folder. Ask Ms. Landry about moving his spot closer to the book shelf for morning carpet.

events.title: Pickup and book-fair envelope
events.notes: Bring booster seat. Envelope has $3 in coins from Grandma; Laura initials the reading sheet before bedtime.

events.title: Quiet break before supper
events.notes: Sesame clip already saved. No store, no camera roll, no comment boxes. Use timer and put away before plates.

events.title: Daniel: online payment + clinic envelope
events.notes: Daniel logs in after supper. Laura keeps Randy's clinic sheet and receipt together in the top drawer. Set out three bowls before bedtime snack.

events.title: Quitman Branch kids rug time
events.notes: Arrive ten minutes early so he can choose two shelves first. Look for fire engines, tractors, snakes, or farm books. Put the take-home card in the same pocket as the school folder.

events.title: Bath, teeth, backpack, little book
events.notes: Check tray choice card in folder, pack clean shirt, put toys in bins, read two pages with finger under each word.

events.title: Kindergarten spring check-in
events.notes: Bring shot card and school form copy. Laura's note: no current bottles to list; mention January warm-forehead night and the playground knee patch.

events.title: Pick up certified copy
events.location: Lincoln Parish Clerk office, Ruston, LA
events.notes: Use Quitman mailing address on request. Check that Aug. 14, 2020 matches school and clinic forms.

events.title: LEGO garage before bath
events.notes: Daddy makes the first hinge. Randy adds the doors and tests the click three times. Laura gives the two-minute bath warning.

events.title: Bath, book, lights out
events.notes: Laura reads dinosaur book. Daniel checks nightlight and closes toolbox. Put cousin toys back in hall basket after weekend.

events.title: Morning field bag
events.notes: Bring cones, water, shin guards. Daniel remind Randy: eyes before feet.

events.title: Frog watch after breakfast
events.notes: Daddy takes first look at the bank. Randy carries the blue net but waits on the grass marker. Hands stay off anything long moving in the weeds.

events.title: Sunday: Randy shirt, quiet ride, napkins
events.notes: White shirt on dresser. Randy puts napkins on table before we leave. Check hands after syrup.

events.title: Pine Grove morning
events.notes: Randy wants the aisle seat near Betty. Ask Ms. Carla if the kids are doing the loud hand-motion song before pickup.

events.title: Birthday lunch at Grandma Betty's
events.notes: Pack Randy's beads from the shoe box for the kids' wagon game. Bring folding chairs and extra napkins; check pot before Randy gets a spoon.

events.title: Class meeting: playground problem cards
events.notes: Card: two kids want same truck. Practice asking teacher, using sand timer, and leaving blocks in shared tub.

events.title: Drop yellow card at school office
events.notes: Mrs. Cole asked for the clinic card before spring break. Daniel checked backpack pocket after breakfast.

events.title: Pickup: cubby art, folder, Mason's truck picture
events.notes: Mrs. Bell said the table group made vehicle drawings. Randy wants to carry Mason's extra picture until Mama asks his parent at pickup.

events.title: Peewee field, snack bags, Eli ride-back
events.notes: Bring shin guards, orange slices, red car. Eli rides back with us if Aunt Kay confirms by 8:30. Yard games at home before naps.

events.title: Quiet tablet choice before errands
events.notes: Timer on. Randy may pick two saved videos: princess sisters song, alphabet puppet clip, or snowman dance. Stop when the bell rings.

events.title: Porch project with Daddy: big crossing + red bay
events.notes: Use gray baseplates, toy helmets, cotton from craft bag, and the Rockies postcard from the fridge.

events.title: Backyard play before supper
events.notes: Set cones from porch steps to sweet gum tree. Keep the little goal away from the driveway. Check laces before they start.
